quest.title: Search in the Algae Sea
quest.description: It's been a while. Time to head back to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and see how everyone's doing with their investigations.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: In the Wake of Narcissus: Act I
chapter.title: Search in the Algae Sea

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You bet we are! Have you found anything new in the meantime?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Mr. Caterpillar and I have been doing some research...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, and...?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: We've discovered that Seymour doesn't, in fact, have an "Annihilation mode."

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Following data fragment sorting, this phrase was found to have been derived from the novel "Prisoner Six: Overrun."

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: In that book, the world organization launched a mass annihilation agent to hunt a chimera down...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that stuff's not important at all!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Apart from using our free time to go out and investigate, we've also read through the books collected here one more time.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: We couldn't make heads or tails of them at first, and even now... Well, they certainly are well-written.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I don't know whose handwriting it is, or what scribe or copyist was hired, but their penmanship is clear and clearly beautiful — a master of calligraphy if I ever saw one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you were talking about the handwriting!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, Paimon's got a bad feeling about this already — did you not find anything during this time, then?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Heh, alright, sorry. I shan't jest any further.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: As you know, we told you all that we found the last time without holding anything back.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: However, I fear that this time, there are some clues hidden in details that we must rely on chance to reveal.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Indeed. For example, if no further revelations concerning a murder emerge, then the blood on a painting will always remain a red smear.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then what would this "chance" be, Caterpillar?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Well... Why don't we do a quick recap of everything we've discovered?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Let's make some deductions regarding what happened in the past — that might give us the opportunity to fill in some gaps that can help us support or refute our views.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: That's a good idea. I've always felt like there's so much about this that's familiar... but I can't recall anything about it.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Negative. I can give a continuous account of the resources that I have sorted—

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Ugh, silly dog. Didn't you only recover your creator's name after talking to us about the matter?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: *mechanical noises* ...Negative. I merely matched similar sounds during said interaction. There was no data loss involved.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: However, I must append that I, too, find that keyword searches make searching for entries more efficient.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, what do we want to discuss?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Well, for a bit of a warmup, or a teaser, if you would—

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: You may be referring to a "heater."

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Yes, that's exactly what I mean — so, let's start off our deductions with something simple.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: What is the "Mary-Ann" in the Annapausis, exactly?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: That "Mary-Ann" holds the greatest secret of all — I'm sure you can see that too.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Let's get ourselves some armchairs, maybe crack open a few beers... Oh, wait, you can't drink yet.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Anyway, let us help you sort our findings out.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I'll start first. Well, the name "Mary-Ann" itself certainly is familiar to me.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: The name of the person I was meant to protect is "Mary-Ann," yes, but I have no data regarding the identity of the one who resides within the Annapausis.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: We are missing context — I can only conclude, based on a human's unmodified lifespan, that they are not the same person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That would seem to be the case, huh? It's been a few hundred years, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, as for Paimon... She ate Chicken-Mushroom Skewer this morning...?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Well, guess it's my turn — you mentioned before that you encountered Oceanid creatures that had a great deal of character... One might say "personality," even.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The precondition for such creatures and their characters is the same — that an intelligent Oceanid has already understood their original forms beforehand.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: So, were you the one who willed those creatures into being, Ann?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, don't you think that's kinda weird — y'know, summoning familiar friends to play house with you for who knows how long and stuff?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Well, I didn't do that! I actually had to get to know Petit Chou, Al, and the others first.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Well, then. In that case, let's see what we can deduce from the things we already know.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: So, regarding Alain's younger sister <color=#00E1FFFF>Mary-Ann</color>, the Annapausis's <color=#00E1FFFF>"Mary-Ann"</color>, the Red Empress <color=#00E1FFFF>Lyris</color>, and the <color=#00E1FFFF>Ann</color> who's with us...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: What will our conclusion be? How will we sustain it, and how shall we refute it?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone gathers.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Is there anything else you feel we should add?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: As I mentioned before, Mary-Ann is not only the Princess in Ann's story, but she is also the person I must protect.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: She is the younger sister of Alain Guillotin, the one who designed me, 4ACV07.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #As for matters concerning me, I suppose you already know all about them, Knight {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, didn't we also hear all sorts of stuff while we were in Elynas?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seymour was also damaged during that time...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: How did it go? Did you think of anything?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: So, could you tell us what you heard?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Perhaps a hilichurl might hear something that humans and Oceanids will not, just as how dogs and humans differ in that regard.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I must correct your statement. My auditory components can indeed pick up higher and lower frequencies as compared to humans. However, I am not a dog. Moreover, a dog's low-frequency hearing is similar to that of a human.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Is that so? Well, I was talking about real dogs, not you, 4ACV07.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Haha, silly dog!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #That said, I didn't think you would hear it too, Knight {NICKNAME}. I wonder if we'd heard the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "But everyone's left..."

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: "They won't come back, no matter how long I wait..."

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Looks like we heard the same thing. I suspect that this was the inner voice of "Mary-Ann."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #Did she say anything else? I'm not trying to invade anyone's privacy or anything. I just think that we're onto something here with you mentioning these words, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Let me think... After that, I also heard something like "I prefer the story of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team sitting down happily for tea time after their adventure has ended."

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: And then...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: "I don't want to hear your stories... I prefer my version."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #...Have you noticed something off about this, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Please state your case.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Let's think our own thoughts through first. Perhaps we really might be able to come to some conclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: We're back again. This time, I must... Mary-Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That's the spirit, Ms. Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: In truth, I must confess to being somewhat jealous of you.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: You still hold out hope of recovering your past. I've... been searching for centuries, but I haven't found a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: So please, do your best for this old caterpillar's part as well, alright? Figure your past out, and come to accept your present self.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yup, I will!

talks.objective: Talk to Caterpillar when you're ready

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That's enough for now. More than enough for a warm-up.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Correct. The oddities in Annapausis all point to the <color=#00E1FFFF>powers of the Oceanids</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But this is not Miss Ann's doing. All of this together means...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's another Oceanid in Annapausis?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That is what I suspect. <color=#00E1FFFF>An Oceanid with whom Mary-Ann has a close relationship</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Or perhaps, she could even be... the princess herself.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Do you mean to say that <color=#00E1FFFF>"Mary-Ann" may, in fact, be Princess Lyris</color>?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Yes, Lyris. The Red Empress of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo from back then, the Red Empress who loves to take heads.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Take heads!?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I seem to have a vague recollection of something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But it's not a story about Lyris. Rather, it's a fairytale about someone named Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Yes. The taking heads thing is just a metaphor. <color=#00E1FFFF>Lyris is made of pure water and so has the ability to dissolve and extract people's wills</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo used her to extract the ego and become holy.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Searching for the keyword "Lyris" has yielded relevant information in my indices.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Talking of the Red Empress has reminded me of a few things about Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Mull that over a while first, then speak to Miss Ann and Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: See if the conclusion you reach awakens any new memories.

talks.objective: Collect more leads and gather your thoughts

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Knight {NICKNAME}, I've remembered the name "Mary-Ann."

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: It's familiar to me because it's from a children's story. The same one that the "Red Empress" comes from.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: The female lead, Liddell, was mistaken for Mary-Ann, the servant. And Mary-Ann never appeared throughout the entire story.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Maybe <color=#00E1FFFF>"Mary-Ann" never really existed... except as a figment in someone's dreams</color>.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How do you know about this story, Ann?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: And isn't that a good question? How do I know about it?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: The memory feels more vivid than those I have of the story of the evil dragon, Narcissus.

talks.objective: Collect more leads and gather your thoughts

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Shall I summarize the entries regarding Lyris I possess for you two?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Omitting the standard citation format. Reconstructing output to match format "report to superiors"...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Lyris is a registered Oceanid. She is not eligible to be stationed in the waters outside Fontaine and has become...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: A special source of information for the nation. She was appointed as the director of an orphanage to symbolize the love and affection of the previous Hydro Archon.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: The orphanage's affairs were mainly managed by its human vice director.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An orphanage director... Then how is she connected to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: As Director, Lyris was very affectionate towards the children and quite devoted to them, but <color=#00E1FFFF>her intelligence among Oceanids was below average</color>.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>She wasn't very good at working out the cause and effect of things, nor could she even count</color>. As a result, she was not qualified to perform covert investigations.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aww, sounds kinda like a big ol' cat mom who can't count!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, because cats can't count, so they pick up their kittens one by one, and keep going back until they see there aren't any kittens left!

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Later, the orphanage was destroyed during the calamity, and official records of her stop there.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: They say she failed to understand the link between the disaster, the orphans fleeing, and her own conduct, and so she wanders the ruins, drowning in guilt and expectation.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I have an underwater locomotion module. Once, Mary-Ann and I... dove down to the ruins of the orphanage, whose coordinates were the same as those of Annapausis.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: There, we found an Oceanid swimming sadly in circles...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: When she next appeared in the records, she was a core member of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and the subject of a high-priority arrest warrant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, but she doesn't seem like a bad person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Considering that she may be connected to Ann, she must've been tricked.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Ah, yes. There's another important piece of information worth noting. The orphanage's name was—

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: The Narzissenkreuz Institute.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Narzissenkreuz...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: These are all Marechaussee Phantom files that Mr. Alain Guillotin recorded for testing light sensitivity while designing me. The output is via my image-to-text-to-speech module.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: According to eyewitness testimony regarding who I suspect to be Lyris, there shouldn't be any problems.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: And you may have heard of this elsewhere, but it's worth mentioning again:

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Alain and Mary-Ann were orphans in the care of the Narzissenkreuz Institute before the Marechaussee Hunter, Emanuel Guillotin, took them in.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you, Seymour.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: #Don't mention it, Noble {M#Sir}{F#Madam}.

talks.objective: Collect more leads and gather your thoughts

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon feels like you've changed a lot since we met in the Fortress of Meropide, Caterpillar...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Would a five-year-old child and a fifteen-year-old teenager be the same? Perhaps returning here simply reminds me of the past, and of who I used to be.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Time is frozen in the Fortress. Being locked up there for a day, or a hundred years... I'm afraid it made no difference to me.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Lanoire is what made time flow for me. Watching her grow reminded me that time still passes, and life is still being born, shining brilliantly, and then being extinguished.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And so I changed as well. That said, my past self — the person I was before I met her — would certainly be more helpful to Ann and Seymour in our current situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Haha! Don't be like that, Paimon! Just think about it — making up stories for Lanoire was nothing more than putting such ways of thinking to good use.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #Regardless, it has nothing to do with the current situation. You look like you still have questions, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Since we have our own suspicions about Ann and Lyris's relationship, we have topics of discussion that can be used to refute or sustain those conjectures.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do Oceanids reproduce?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm sure you have friends more knowledgeable than I am regarding that. Perhaps you can even find scholars of natural philosophy who have dedicated research to the question.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Or you could have asked the Oceanids you know personally... but you asked me.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Of course, I know what you mean. So this is your speculation? I see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't get it.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #When we exchanged information earlier, {NICKNAME} mentioned that <color=#00E1FFFF>Ann is the person in "Mary-Ann's" dream</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Or perhaps, she might be a manifestation made by "Mary-Ann" — an Oceanid-Oceanid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oceanid-Oceanid? Why the repetition? ...Are you just trying to make it sound cuter?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Apologies, perhaps my description was ill-done. Still, can an Oceanid create an Oceanid-creature version of an Oceanid?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's deep! That's like asking if hard candies can be used as the filler for another hard candy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what would you say to that? This question's really interesting, but Paimon's already hungry for answers!

choices.text: I suppose I'd have to say...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Still, you may not realize just how deep this rabbit hole goes, so let me explain.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do tell.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: You might be confused as to why there are Oceanid creatures with personalities in the Annapausis.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: If Oceanids can create Oceanid creatures, then can they create Oceanid-Humans or Oceanid-Oceanids?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Convention dictates that it's rare for Oceanids to be able to mimic a human, unless the human drowns in their arms, or the Oceanid has spent extensive time with the person and knows everything about them.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: And the Oceanid in question must also have tremendous wisdom and compassion. I'm afraid perhaps only one as powerful as Rhodeia could do it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, so that means Idyia must be incredibly strong...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: So it's rare to mimic humans, but not impossible. Now, creating another Oceanid... That's different.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Creating humans using human knowledge can only be achieved by gods, and the same applies to Oceanids creating Oceanids. It usually should be impossible — in this world, at least.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Unless... Unless this human or Oceanid has already placed themselves above their own kind, and attempted such insanity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean... They thought they had become a god?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: That's right. Followers blindly believe in their leaders, who in turn blindly believe in themselves, giving rise to delirium and delusions.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: "I can do what a god can do. Their deeds are not that great, after all."

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: A powerful belief is also a powerful will, and magic is a skill that molds reality to your will.

choices.text: Perhaps the descendant hypothesis makes more sense.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Perhaps, perhaps! It's possible, and quite understandable, too.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: If nothing else, the Lyris I know doesn't have this kind of intelligence... nor would she be this crazy.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I have some... less mainstream ideas about how Oceanids reproduce, but they're not important, and we can discuss them later.

choices.text: Perhaps "Mary-Ann" doesn't consider herself an Oceanid-type?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I am very sorry. I may be unable to offer any logical support at this time.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My listening equipment cannot hear inner voices.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry, you've helped plenty already.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Could you tell me your assessment? Is the Mary-Ann from Annapausis the person I am meant to protect or not?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I am willing to believe your judgment, even if that means I have to update my data.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: According to my records, Mary-Ann Guillotin never exhibited the behavior of waiting for others to come back after the Narzissenkreuz Institute was destroyed.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: That means she must have returned to the ruins here after being adopted, living there for a while. But there is no possible timeframe that meets these requirements.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: ...Logical error, data fragment sorting initiated...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I trust your judgment. However...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: "I prefer the story of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team sitting down happily for tea time after their adventure has ended."

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: It seems that she, too, was an orphan from the Narzissenkreuz Institute, but other relevant information cannot be matched to her.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: ...Logical error, data fragment sorting initiated...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The "Mary-Ann" in Annapausis...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That makes her our prime suspect, then.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: To be honest, were you using the process of elimination, you actually already guessed as much long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I didn't want to disrespect Ann, though.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: You're right. But you do already have a version of the story in your heart — your own interpretation, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If that's the case, then we should go find that "Mary-Ann," and see for ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Please permit me to change the topic for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Does this mean that I shall no longer be able to fulfill my orders to protect Mary-Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've worked out this much, and that's the only bit you care about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, it may be cruel, but from the moment we discovered that the Guillotin siblings were from centuries ago, it was probably inevitable...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Correction. So, the conclusion would be that it was my incompetence that exposed Mary-Ann to danger?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Do not blame yourself. You have fought to the point of destruction. You have done your part.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: There's no need to be so pessimistic either. Though that is an odd thing to say to a machine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. It's like pouring Fonta into a sink and then saying "Sink, you'll get fat if you keep drinking like this!"

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Oh. 4ACV07.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't believe you remember that...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: What is it, Mr. Caterpillar? Why use my official designation?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: We may not have reached any conclusions. But we now know what to do next.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Look. There is a Mary-Ann in Annapausis too, and she also has close links to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My long-term memory module confirms this.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: As such, there's no need to restore your logic module to factory settings yet. Let's take a step back.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: We can still go and find this Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Thank you for your logical troubleshooting and... emotional adaptive maintenance.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I think... what you said makes sense. It is not yet time to admit defeat and restore myself to my initial settings in order to take on a new mission.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yeah! That's right, you silly doggy!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Let's leave things here for a while, then. Once you are ready, we can continue.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Hmm. Why don't we go find this Mary-Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Let's solve that mystery before tackling the Narzissenkreuz Ordo issue.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Mmhmm. I'd really like to figure that one out too. After all, it might explain where I come from.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: My logic module agrees that this is the correct course of action.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: So, shall we go then?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Hmm? I gather that some things happened over there, then?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #Oh, we just ran into "immunity"-related issues often due to Knight {NICKNAME}'s Hydro resonance, that's all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels like some extraordinary instinct awakened in you after you met Seymour, Ann...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Is it time to review responsibilities and apportion blame? I do not think I should be held accountable, for I can only override my protective prerogative in moments of great danger.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #Don't worry, Knight {NICKNAME}. We'll make "Mary-Ann" tell us everything this time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! What are these guys doing here again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! Isn't that Al's group?

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: #Hohoho! Yes, it is us. And you are... Knight {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: It's really good to see you. So good that I can't control myself anymore. Please dodge to the best of your ability.

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: She asked us to send you a message. Now let me take out her handwritten letter with my hands, which are much like yours, yellow and white ones. Ahem—

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: "I don't want to hear your stories... I prefer my version."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got it, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: There are four Seals in total. If my hypothesis is correct, then they should be at these locations, respectively...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? These four locations...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've been to some of them before during our adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I see. And did you find anything there?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You describe your adventures there.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: ...I see. This proves two things. Firstly, my hypothesis is accurate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And the other?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Secondly, the situation is grim. We need to get moving and see if we still have a chance to turn things around.

talks.objective: Stop Al and Jak, who have lost control

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got it, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: There are four Seals in total. If my hypothesis is correct, then they should be at these locations, respectively...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? These four locations...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've been to them during our adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, to be precise, we've been to three out of the four locations.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I see. And did you find anything there?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You describe your adventures there.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: ...I see. This proves two things. Firstly, my hypothesis is accurate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And the other?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The situation is grim. We must hurry to the fourth location.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. The bubble that was here before is gone, too.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Well, it was Princess Lyris's magic... That's just how the story goes.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Let me think of a way.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Close your eyes, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: A temporary optical sensor shutdown? Understood. They will be reactivated on your command.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, why do we have to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The essence of a mime is pretense — the charade that something is still here.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And belief is the heart of magic, the faith that there is meaning here... so, let's close our eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: So, Ann, begin imagining what it would look like if that bubble was still here.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You close your eyes, and feel some sort of fluctuation...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "I prefer the story of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team sitting down happily for tea time after their adventure has ended."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it really appeared!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The Ordo called this step, the process of imagining something in such detail, "imaging."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go over and have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about what happened previously.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Hmm. You didn't go ahead and save the world while we split up to investigate, now did you?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: A lot has happened indeed. It's no wonder you've forgotten what we went through together.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I jest, of course. Maybe you're just tired, and it's eluding you for now.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: To put it simply, we met in the Fortress of Meropide, and you helped me rescue Lanoire.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And now, it's my turn to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? It's the entrance that's disappeared this time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ann, do you know to make the portal... Uh, can you do your "imaging" thing on it?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Alright. Let me give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You close your eyes, and a lonesome silence comes over you...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "But everyone's left. They won't come back, no matter how long I wait..."

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I can't... it seems...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, why?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How are we supposed to see Mary-Ann, then?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I suspect that this is because the portal has lost meaning, and thus cannot be recreated.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: From what you told me before, the entrance that was once placed here led to a story that had yet to be written.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Now that she has said everything she wanted to, the story no longer has any meaning. Mary-Ann is rejecting our answer, and that is why the way in is shut.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does... Does this mean we're going to return empty-handed?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It does seem so.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I wouldn't say we're completely out of luck.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Did you notice something we didn't then, Knight {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I heard something while Ann was "imaging."

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I did hear something then... So you can hear it too?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Would that be Mary-Ann's real thoughts?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: What did you two hear?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Ah, hmm, might be best not to discuss personal secrets here — the walls might have ears and all. Let's head back before talking about this.

talks.objective: Talk to Caterpillar when you're ready

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: We've put the pieces of the case that were floating all over the algae sea back together.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's just an empty box even after being put together, but we've finally figured out...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: What the lost pearl should look like.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhm, what are you trying to say, Caterpillar?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait. Don't give Paimon any hints. She's gonna figure this out on her own!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We pieced together a good guess from the clues, but the truth is... still unproven?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Of course. My speech analysis module has determined that Miss Paimon is correct.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Actually, I meant that we may never know the truth. But I'm afraid we have no choice but to accept this conjecture.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #So, Knight {NICKNAME}, is this the secret of my birth?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: It's... I'm afraid I can't... accept something like this right away...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I understand, Ms. Ann. It's a shocking fact, and it'll require you to accept yourself again.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But I don't think it should be that difficult to do so. After all, knowing your past does not require abandoning everything about the present.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I do not understand the specific context of this discussion. But I would like to add that I do not believe I am different from how I was before suffering disk damage.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Even though you insist on addressing me as a silly dog, my identification number is still 4ACV07.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Come on, it's not that serious! I promised Knight {NICKNAME} that I would accept this conclusion, as long as it's reasonable.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Then I have a suggestion, one that will resolve Miss Ann's quandary and put a stop to Narzissenkreuz's plans.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Narzissenkreuz...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Narzissen... Oh! Paimon remembers now! You mentioned him before, Caterpillar. Just who is he, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well... Simply put, the leader of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Sounds like he's got an impressive resume! But isn't the Narzissenkreuz Ordo always up to no good? Wouldn't that make him the nastiest of the lot?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Of course. During my time with my master, creator, and the other Marechaussee Hunters, we devoted most of our time to hunting the Ordo down.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: As I said before, the goal of the Elynas operation was to capture or eliminate Narzissenkreuz as well. However, my memory does not contain any intelligence regarding his involvement.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That's a given. Looking back at it now, he was merely using us as bait. And I wasn't the only one... It was the same for Jakob, Lyris, and many others in the Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm afraid the Elynas operation was probably never more than a red herring with the goal of leading you and Guillotin away to buy him more time to execute his true plans.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Remember the Doomsday Clock I mentioned?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's what the Ordo considers the countdown to the apocalypse, right?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: To be more precise, it's the apocalypse as calculated by the world-formula. This planet itself should survive just fine, though...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: "The beast of the stars shall drink the amniotic fluid of the world dry. A hundred years more, and all surface life shall be wiped away."

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Once life on the surface is wiped out, only that which is underwater will remain. Can a planet full of fish eventually rise up to the ocean of stars?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The thought of all terrestrial life going extinct is pretty spooky, but when you say things like that, it does give things a romantic ring...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: It's the heading of a Yae Publishing House novel from a few years back. Mamere brought it back to the village to learn how to paint.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: O—Oh, no wonder...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Anyways, for myself and the others gathered here, though the Narzissenkreuz Ordo is the source of all our troubles...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Its objective and Narzissenkreuz's great purpose are actually completely selfless.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: He only took the actions he did because he calculated the coming of the apocalypse. He wishes to save the world.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: So is the world really on the verge of destruction?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I believe this to be a pathological delusion caused by paranoia.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Were the apocalypse real... would you be able to forgive Narzissenkreuz?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: No. It's a bit too early to consider such things. You have yet to understand what happened to you, Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And as for you, Seymour, your hostility is a result of your programming and the duties it imposes.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I suppose we must find the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Holy Blade... of Narzissenkreuz?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm talking about the real one, of course... as much as it may be quite strange to say that the ceremonial sword of a magic society is real.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Not only will it help us stop Narzissenkreuz's plans, but its unique powers may be able to undo the merging of wills.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: We should be able to separate Lyris and Mary-Ann. And then, Miss Ann, you can defeat the evil dragon, Narcissus, and rescue Princess Lyris.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Regardless...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Let's get moving first.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That's the spirit. It might take some time to explain, so let's move out first and I'll explain when we get there.

talks.objective: Follow Caterpillar's directions to the specified location

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Atmospheric visibility is acceptable today... Enough that you can see that tower over there, yes?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: That building was once known to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo as the "Tower of Ipsissimus," but we would later call it the "Tower of Gestalt."

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: It was named for the idea that things that have been separated need to be combined to display their original, complete form.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: But I suppose I might be speaking in reverse. The heart was complete to begin with — and the mistake was to divide it up for separate study.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Paimon didn't get a thing you said.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: It's fine, don't worry about it. Plays on words are also a trick that mysterious organizations enjoy pulling. What matters is what we must do next.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Some of the vocabulary you used is missing from my semantic indexes, so I could not properly parse your meaning.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: But I understood the last sentence. Please tell me what I should do.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: While investigating alone, I found a map of the Seal of Chymical Marriage. You could say that I've found four seals.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: And this tower is one of the locations?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: That's not the place we need to go. That said, though, who can be sure? Perhaps our destinies will yet take us there in the future.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Either way, we need to use the position of the tower to locate the other four places. That's why we've come here first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what are those four seals for?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, we've discovered from experience that it's usually best practice to just break the seals and give whatever ringleader we find a good walloping.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: As for me, I'd like to restore the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: It's more for ceremonial use. But it could be used as a weapon, I guess...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Well, I suppose we could also just call it "the answer."

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: As I've said before, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo once had a ceremony to remove the ego and will.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The Holy Blade was used in that ritual.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I remember something about that...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: If Lyris and Mary-Ann's wills created Ann... And if the old me was placed in some Hilichurl's body...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Aah!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Wait a minute. Didn't we already find the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: What? Really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look!

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: A wooden sword.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: It's the wooden sword we found during our adventures.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Hmm, yes, so it is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! What kind of reaction is that?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Perhaps you can think of it like this. That's a wooden sword found in the Narzissenkreuz Institute, named the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz. That makes it more important than any ordinary wooden sword.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Perhaps it might be of use when the time is right, just like the Holy Blade in the story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? You don't need to try to make us feel better...

choices.text: I passed it by earlier, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got it, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Anyway, assuming I looked at the map from the right angle, we will find the entrance to one of the Seals nearby.

talks.objective: Find and break the four Seals

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then we ended up at the top of that Tower of Gestalt place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're separated from Caterpillar, Ann, and Seymour...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What should we do? It looks like there are traps waiting down below.

choices.text: Things haven't gotten serious yet. Let's check out the scenery.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, you should have at least a little sense of urgency!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows you're a good fighter, but Paimon's worried about the others.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But our only choice is to keep going... Oh, is that the entrance?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If there's any traps, just smash 'em!

choices.text: It's not dangerous yet. Let's count some prime numbers.

talks.objective: Find and break the four Seals

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I was worried the Master's clock might break down at a crucial moment, so I came just to do a bit of maintenance.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: What took you so long? I've even had time to finish the anti-rust treatment and oil it up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the voice we heard earlier! You're... uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Purple Dude!

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: ...I've told you, just call me Jakob.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did you set up this trap?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I believe the "Persona" section to be the most important, for there lies the persona excised by Master Narzissenkreuz himself.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Only a drop of water from an Oceanid can open it. I can't allow it to be taken by just any ignorant adventurer.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: So I set a trap before activating the Orthant and sealed the space off.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why are you here?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Why shouldn't I be here? This is a Narzissenkreuz Ordo base. Is there something wrong with returning to my own base?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: You're the ones who are trespassing. Don't you feel even a twinge of guilt for breaking the law?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: "This was once the realm of a god. Now, a pheasant sits upon the throne." Just like the world today.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: As compensation, give me the rest of your paints and the "Persona" I need.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I refuse.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Even now, at a time like this... Just what are you so hung up on?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The countdown to the world's end has started. I must forge the Holy Blade and place it in my Master's hand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is Narzissenkreuz this "Master" of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Indeed. According to his world-formula, the second deluge is looming before us. When it comes, only he will be able to save the world.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Only by forging the Holy Blade can he continue his unfinished work, gathering the wills of everyone in Fontaine, the continent, and even the entire planet unto himself.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: As the primordial sea returns once more, and as the devourer of all darkens the sky, only he who is whole unto himself may survive.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Only then will all of our souls — nay, all of humanity's souls — be spared from destruction. We will welcome a new dawn in the tranquil sea of innocence he grants us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is your big plan to save the world?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It sounds like you're just bundling everyone's consciousness together without consent.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: And what would you know of anything? Only Master Narzissenkreuz's new body will survive the coming of the second deluge.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Even if all other life disappears into the sea, he will survive alone. He will remember all those lives that were lost.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: He recognizes the value and equality of all life — a selflessness that shall not be besmirched by ones such as you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So where is he now?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: In the deepest depths beneath us. When the thugs and dogs of Fontaine surrounded us and attempted to wipe us out, he descended alone into the abyss below.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: But he must still be alive, and the time for his return is nigh.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Quickly, give me what you have on you. Then I will have all the Orthants, and you may leave.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: How about this? I will trade you this rust treatment and oil. Think of it as a gift for that foolish dog.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: In the dawn of the new world, it is unlikely there will be a place for it or Guillotin's fantasies.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I refuse. The world is not as weak as you think.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That's right! Paimon and {NICKNAME} have seen more crises than you've eaten Lotus Flower Crisps. And we always come out on top!

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Truly, there is no reaching your exalted heights.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I remember how the Master used to pretend to be an evil dragon when we played as children.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Who would have thought he would become the hero, while the real evil dragons would come at us, one after another.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Guillotin may have disappeared, but here his successors come, self-assured, thinking themselves totally infallible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the heck are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The time has come. A century ago, the prophecy predicted all. He will return.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: If you will not give me what I need willingly, I will take it myself.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If my sense of direction is right, I'm afraid the interior of the Tower of Gestalt is below us now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've never been there, Caterpillar?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It is the closest point to Master's ultimate goal. I do not believe many have been there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That means we don't know what we'll find there.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm ashamed to admit it, but yes.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: What... What's all this?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Warning. Abnormal environmental changes detected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can see that just fine!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It seems we don't have much time. Let's get to work, quickly!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Before Jakob's new world becomes a reality.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a huge mechanical core.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: How shall we descend?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: An optical-coupling design, is it? It looks like we need to get all the rays to hit their targets.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So how do we do that?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: There must be some kind of equipment nearby. Have a look around.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? It's already starting?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me think back on what's happened.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #Let me know if I can be of assistance in any way, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob

dialogues.speaker: Jakob

dialogues.text: I was nothing more than your "exhibit" at that time, nor could I understand your grand plans. Plus, I tend to have a bad memory for things I don't like.

dialogues.text: But on your return, you performed the "Dispelling Ritual." How fastidious of you.

dialogues.text: Of course. How could I allow spiritual impurities or contaminants into the Master's space?

dialogues.text: Alas, you have not yet left your cocoon. You will return to the void in the end. There is no place for you in the new world.

dialogues.text: Hand over the rest of it.

dialogues.text: Hmph. I shall permit it. It seems it is you who are the hero wielding the Holy Blade in this telling of the story, while I am the dragon who falls to your sword.

dialogues.text: It matters not in the end. All the elements are in place and the dragon has been defeated. You may guard "reason" — for now.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: After all, nobody can truly own the Holy Blade. We merely hold it as it travels in the direction it must, until it reaches its final destiny.

dialogues.text: The Holy Blade can be any object. But there is particular symbolism in it being a sword.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well then, present something that can hold "reason."

dialogues.text: Let's use the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz we found earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: *nod*

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Th—This is...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: What's next, Jakob?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Eh? Uh... Hm.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Don't you want to reforge the Holy Blade as soon as possible?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Next, Oceanid, you touch the sword.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...Is this a trap?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: No. Although the Holy Blade can part any will from water, it can also unite wills. It can accommodate both the primordial, and that of order.

dialogues.text: You have been chosen because even if you are an illusion, you contain something that the Narzissenkreuz Ordo has gathered over many years...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: ...The power of will.

dialogues.text: Should we trust him?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: His biological indicators show a very low probability of lying, though I remain doubtful.

dialogues.text: How long must you dawdle? You're no better than that rusty old shell Guillotin created.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Would you like some oil for your brain? Or rust remover?

dialogues.text: Speaking of rust remover...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That watch...

dialogues.text: Yeah! We can try using rust remover on the watch!

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: What nonsense are you all going on about...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Adults shouldn't interrupt children.

dialogues.text: And I'm a child, too.

dialogues.text: Whoa! It's open!

dialogues.text: And there's... a photo inside?

dialogues.text: Hmm. How nostalgic. Alain, Rene, Director Lyris, Mary-Ann, and myself, as we once were.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I... I remember this photo...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I think I remember...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Well? Has the oil helped lubricate your rusty decision-making skills?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: If we don't take this step, we'll never be able to leave the world of memory.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yeah. Let me give it a try, then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: It's okay. I've made up my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.text: Is this what the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz is really like?

dialogues.text: Weren't you listening? Caterpillar just explained that the Holy Blade can indwell any form that holds significance.

dialogues.text: Ah... Just like the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz we imagined...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You changed back!

dialogues.text: Ahem... Very good. My mission is complete. Now, I propose a trade.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Now, you, Oceanid! Please take all my emotions and memories.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: My power is no match for yours, and I will soon disappear.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Save all that I am, that I may be reunited with everyone in the new world.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Seems like he's not up-to-date with the latest news...)

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: We established several nodes in Fontaine in accordance with the Seal of Chymical Marriage as part of our response to the apocalypse.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Today, only the five most important survive. Only the smallest part of our Master's plan has been implemented, but even that is a form of success.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The arrival of the new world is fated. I...

dialogues.text: I cannot absorb your persona and memories. After all, I have no wish to retain anyone as with such serious sins on their hands as you are now.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.text: You may no longer be the crybaby Jakob, but as you are now, you are still not worthy of eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Rather than do that, we will help you and treat you. You must atone for your sins.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Part of the Red Empress is within you, so you should know that she rejected the future.

dialogues.text: I do not wish to do so. And I will persuade that part of Lyris, too.

dialogues.text: The appointed time has come. It seems the watch wound up running a little fast over the course of a century.

dialogues.text: What's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I have reversed the Seal of Chymical Marriage and reforged the Holy Blade of Reason. The truth of the world-formula has been proven.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The Seal of Chymical Marriage was an ancient Fontainian ritual meant to seal off the source of life. Now it has been reversed, and all has been set free once more!

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: Now, it is time for our Master... No, for Rene to return!

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: He will break the seal and control the source of life. The pure water of life will inundate the world as he rises once more, giving birth to a new universe.

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: All souls will be preserved forever, and the Blade of Will shall fall into the waters and be grasped by its legitimate owner.

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: All will be united as one, and gain the power to combat the apocalypse.

response.text: Jakob!

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: It may take Master a little time to find my will in the new world. But do not worry. We will meet there again!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Jakob!

choices.text: Wait. Back in the Fortress of Meropide, the Primordial Sea was...

dialogues.text: What a terrible ending... But I fear there's little time for mourning or lamentation. Everything now hangs by a thread.

dialogues.text: Is that the "Persona" piece ahead?

dialogues.text: Unable to analyze the density of the substance before us. It appears to have a mass of... zero.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It looks like we've got the last piece. We should at least be able to negotiate a bit with our opposition now.

dialogues.text: On the bright side, at least we can stop the Narzissenkreuz Ordo from forging the Holy Blade.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Not at all, Paimon. Our final goal is to forge the Holy Blade ourselves, and use it to stop their plan.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Of course, Ann, I have not forgotten what this sword means to you.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: A Holy Sword that can cut out the will is also your key to unraveling the mystery. And to be honest, it is equally important to me as well.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's just that we have more important, more pressing matters at hand. Would you mind, then, if we looked into the mysteries surrounding us later?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I'm fine with that.

dialogues.text: Are you ready to begin?

dialogues.text: You don't seem to want to link the two of them together.

dialogues.text: What a coincidence. I happen to agree.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But I have some other thoughts to share too, though they may have nothing to do with the next step in our reasoning.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Are you willing to listen?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm listening.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Earlier, we broached the topic of Oceanid reproduction.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's a huge taboo for Oceanids to mimic and transform into one of their own kind, just as it is for humans to create humans.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But you see... Humans can create humans. Through love.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: "Go. Pursue eternity, not through mystery, but love."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: What if, by some chance, this mysterious method of Oceanid reproduction is accomplished through imagination and mimicry?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Perhaps their regret or remorse gives birth to a thought, and as they imagine the path that could have been taken, a new Oceanid is born.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's a very interesting idea.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: We'll never know. After all, it's a secret passed down amongst Oceanids only.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: In any case, we'll begin once you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Player

dialogues.text: I'm looking forward to it.

dialogues.text: It's okay. I've made up my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Ann

dialogues.speaker: Jakob

dialogues.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Ahem... Very good. My mission is complete. Now, I propose a trade.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Now, you, Oceanid! Please take all my emotions and memories.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: My power is no match for yours, and I will soon disappear.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Save all that I am, that I may be reunited with everyone in the new world.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: We established several nodes in Fontaine in accordance with the Seal of Chymical Marriage as part of our response to the apocalypse.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Today, only the five most important survive. Only the smallest part of our Master's plan has been implemented, but even that is a form of success.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The arrival of the new world is fated. I...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I cannot absorb your persona and memories. After all, I have no wish to retain anyone as with such serious sins on their hands as you are now.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: You may no longer be the crybaby Jakob, but as you are now, you are still not worthy of eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Rather than do that, we will help you and treat you. You must atone for your sins.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Part of the Red Empress is within you, so you should know that she rejected the future.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: She wanted to return to the Narzissenkreuz Institute as it was, and watch again as we pretended to be the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Beautiful memories are the only eternity in this world. There are no others.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Grant it to me, oh being of eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I do not wish to do so. And I will persuade that part of Lyris, too.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The appointed time has come. It seems the watch wound up running a little fast over the course of a century.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: What's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I have reversed the Seal of Chymical Marriage and reforged the Holy Blade of Reason. The truth of the world-formula has been proven.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The Seal of Chymical Marriage was an ancient Fontainian ritual meant to seal off the source of life. Now it has been reversed, and all has been set free once more!

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: Now, it is time for our Master... No, for Rene to return!

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: He will break the seal and control the source of life. The pure water of life will inundate the world as he rises once more, giving birth to a new universe.

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: All souls will be preserved forever, and the Blade of Will shall fall into the waters and be grasped by its legitimate owner.

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: All will be united as one, and gain the power to combat the apocalypse.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Jakob!

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: I've already anticipated the end for this body. "The clock may stop, and its hands fall still."

response.speaker: Jakob
response.text: It may take Master a little time to find my will in the new world. But do not worry. We will meet there again!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Jakob!

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Ha... Ha... It's been a while, "chrysalis." Still no sign of metamorphosis, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Perhaps you've grown too used to being a caterpillar?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Have you already forgotten the time we spent here?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: It was a brief time compared to our eternity. But those brief moments granted us mastery of this universe.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I was nothing more than your "exhibit" at that time, nor could I understand your grand plans. Plus, I tend to have a bad memory for things I don't like.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But on your return, you performed the "Dispelling Ritual." How fastidious of you.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Of course. How could I allow spiritual impurities or contaminants into the Master's space?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Alas, you have not yet left your cocoon. You will return to the void in the end. There is no place for you in the new world.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hand over the rest of it.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Hmph. I shall permit it. It seems it is you who are the hero wielding the Holy Blade in this telling of the story, while I am the dragon who falls to your sword.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: It matters not in the end. All the elements are in place and the dragon has been defeated. You may guard "reason" — for now.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: After all, nobody can truly own the Holy Blade. We merely hold it as it travels in the direction it must, until it reaches its final destiny.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The Holy Blade can be any object. But there is particular symbolism in it being a sword.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well then, present something that can hold "reason."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's use the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz we found earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: *nod*

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Th—This is...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: What's next, Jakob?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Eh? Uh... Hm.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Don't you want to reforge the Holy Blade as soon as possible?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Next, Oceanid, you touch the sword.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...Is this a trap?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: No. Although the Holy Blade can part any will from water, it can also unite wills. It can accommodate both the primordial, and that of order.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: You have been chosen because even if you are an illusion, you contain something that the Narzissenkreuz Ordo has gathered over many years...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: ...The power of will.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Should we trust him?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: His biological indicators show a very low probability of lying, though I remain doubtful.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: How long must you dawdle? You're no better than that rusty old shell Guillotin created.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Would you like some oil for your brain? Or rust remover?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Speaking of rust remover...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That watch...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We can try using rust remover on the watch!

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: What nonsense are you all going on about...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Adults shouldn't interrupt children.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And I'm a child, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! It's open!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And there's... a photo inside?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Hmm. How nostalgic. Alain, Rene, Director Lyris, Mary-Ann, and myself, as we once were.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I... I remember this photo...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I think I remember...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Matching traits detected. That is Mary-Ann, my ward.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Well? Has the oil helped lubricate your rusty decision-making skills?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: If we don't take this step, we'll never be able to leave the world of memory.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yeah. Let me give it a try, then.
