dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon feels like you've changed a lot since we met in the Fortress of Meropide, Caterpillar...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Would a five-year-old child and a fifteen-year-old teenager be the same? Perhaps returning here simply reminds me of the past, and of who I used to be.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Time is frozen in the Fortress. Being locked up there for a day, or a hundred years... I'm afraid it made no difference to me.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Lanoire is what made time flow for me. Watching her grow reminded me that time still passes, and life is still being born, shining brilliantly, and then being extinguished.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And so I changed as well. That said, my past self — the person I was before I met her — would certainly be more helpful to Ann and Seymour in our current situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Haha! Don't be like that, Paimon! Just think about it — making up stories for Lanoire was nothing more than putting such ways of thinking to good use.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #Regardless, it has nothing to do with the current situation. You look like you still have questions, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Since we have our own suspicions about Ann and Lyris's relationship, we have topics of discussion that can be used to refute or sustain those conjectures.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do Oceanids reproduce?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm sure you have friends more knowledgeable than I am regarding that. Perhaps you can even find scholars of natural philosophy who have dedicated research to the question.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Or you could have asked the Oceanids you know personally... but you asked me.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Of course, I know what you mean. So this is your speculation? I see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't get it.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #When we exchanged information earlier, {NICKNAME} mentioned that <color=#00E1FFFF>Ann is the person in "Mary-Ann's" dream</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Or perhaps, she might be a manifestation made by "Mary-Ann" — an Oceanid-Oceanid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oceanid-Oceanid? Why the repetition? ...Are you just trying to make it sound cuter?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Apologies, perhaps my description was ill-done. Still, can an Oceanid create an Oceanid-creature version of an Oceanid?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's deep! That's like asking if hard candies can be used as the filler for another hard candy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what would you say to that? This question's really interesting, but Paimon's already hungry for answers!

choices.text: I suppose I'd have to say...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Still, you may not realize just how deep this rabbit hole goes, so let me explain.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do tell.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: You might be confused as to why there are Oceanid creatures with personalities in the Annapausis.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: If Oceanids can create Oceanid creatures, then can they create Oceanid-Humans or Oceanid-Oceanids?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Convention dictates that it's rare for Oceanids to be able to mimic a human, unless the human drowns in their arms, or the Oceanid has spent extensive time with the person and knows everything about them.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: And the Oceanid in question must also have tremendous wisdom and compassion. I'm afraid perhaps only one as powerful as Rhodeia could do it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, so that means she must be incredibly strong...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: So it's rare to mimic humans, but not impossible. Now, creating another Oceanid... That's different.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Creating humans using human knowledge can only be achieved by gods, and the same applies to Oceanids creating Oceanids. It usually should be impossible — in this world, at least.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Unless... Unless this human or Oceanid has already placed themselves above their own kind, and attempted such insanity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean... They thought they had become a god?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: That's right. Followers blindly believe in their leaders, who in turn blindly believe in themselves, giving rise to delirium and delusions.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: "I can do what a god can do. Their deeds are not that great, after all."

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: A powerful belief is also a powerful will, and magic is a skill that molds reality to your will.

choices.text: Perhaps the descendant hypothesis makes more sense.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Perhaps, perhaps! It's possible, and quite understandable, too.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: If nothing else, the Lyris I know doesn't have this kind of intelligence... nor would she be this crazy.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I have some... less mainstream ideas about how Oceanids reproduce, but they're not important, and we can discuss them later.

choices.text: Perhaps "Mary-Ann" doesn't consider herself an Oceanid-type?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hold on.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Sure, mull it over for a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Logical error. Sorting data fragments...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Please do not be concerned. After warming up, fragment sorting speed will be greatly enhanced.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: The process should be complete before you begin speculating.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Knight {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything else you want to say?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I'm just an Oceanid who doesn't know anything, and I'm really bad at thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Even if you just told me a random story, I'd still believe it all, hook, line, and sinker. The world is too complicated, after all, and I'm not experienced enough to spot any holes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I wouldn't do that.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Thank you, Knight {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I think that the Mary-Ann in Annapausis is the same as me.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: She might look smart, but she doesn't want to accept this complicated world, so she chooses to protect herself with fairy tales.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But even fairy tales must end.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #I believe you, Knight {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Even if your story isn't as happy as Mary-Ann's fairy tales, to me, a tale with an ending is better than a fairy tale without one.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon, do you have any questions for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you refresh my memory on what happened previously?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Um, have you forgotten certain details? Uh, I'm just a little Oceanid, so explaining every little thing might be beyond me...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Anyway, I was determined to rescue Petit Chou when we first met. Luckily, Paimon and you helped.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Later on, we intended to rescue Princess Lyris and defeat the evil dragon. But we met Mary-Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: She told us things I couldn't understand, and it seemed like she was holding on to some very important secret.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #How can I help you, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Command: Recall what happened before.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Of course. You repaired me inside Elynas. I was only capable of repeating a fixed set of lines up until then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon remembers something like that. That was outrageous!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Please forgive me, it was a necessary measure to preserve my internal storage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Forget it! Even Mamere forgave you, so we have no right to stay angry.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Mamere...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I wonder how she's doing. My long-term memory module frequently requests updates for her file.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you trying to say that you miss her?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: That is not imprecise.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: After that, we thwarted the schemes of Jakob of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: And as I must find my ward, Ms. Mary-Ann, I shall be going with you.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: These stories... Just how do I know them...?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: By the way, in the end, everything was the Red Empress's dream, and the Red Queen was merely a cat.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I hope my information helps.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Now, let's reorganize the information that everyone just recalled. This might take quite some time, and might be somewhat hard on our throats.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Then let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me think it over...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That's a good idea. Do think about it first, then.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Oceanid reproduction?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The popular view is that Oceanids somehow managed to split the helix that represents life within them.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Newborn Oceanids are ignorant and innocent, yet the same cannot be said for Oceanid creatures.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I have my own thoughts on the subject, though it's a long story.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the damage to Seymour and Elynas...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, Seymour was damaged inside Elynas, and Mamere's been taking care of him!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: To my shame, yes... Though I do not have such emotions, you can see it as me having lowered my assessment of myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And according to Elynas, the battle that occurred within his body ended quite terribly.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Evidently, that was the battle that damaged you, and it was an incredibly fierce one. But considering that you were damaged...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Then your master might've been...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Common sense dictates that <color=#00E1FFFF>the fate of Mary-Ann Guillotin, sister of Alain Guillotin, was most likely a grim one</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But this world is full of tales of loyal knights who exchanged their lives for a miracle, so you needn't grieve too much, Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: (Seymour appears to have entered data fragment sorting mode out of pure shock.)

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But your master, Mary-Ann, was an <color=#00E1FFFF>ordinary human being</color>, wasn't she? And the time that has passed since then far surpasses the lifespan of any human...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: How did it go? Did you think of anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The "Red Empress" Lyris...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: She was an important figure in the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, and she is also the other Oceanid involved in the tale apart from Ms. Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: One of only two Oceanids... and we also just agreed that we believe there must be an Oceanid behind Annapausis.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But her traits don't match those of the "Mary-Ann" we encountered.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Could it be that Lyris's imagination was behind everything, even me?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That's unlikely. Seymour mentioned that her intelligence was quite limited, so phantoms of this sort would be quite hard for her — similar to how an author would struggle to write a character more intelligent than themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: In fairy tales, the kitten may dream of their living little master, but I fear such things don't happen much in real life.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: So, who is behind all this? And who in the world is that "Mary-Ann"?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: How did it go? Did you think of anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Oceanid Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Huh? What about me, again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We once suspected that you might be the person that "Mary-Ann" dreamed of.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, in your view, "Mary-Ann" is the Oceanid behind the curtain, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I... I don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well then, do you find the name Lyris familiar? She is, after all, the only Oceanid involved in this apart from yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: If you mean the title, "The Red Empress," then yes, I do have some impression of it.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: How did it go? Did you think of anything?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Chicken-Mushroom Skewer. At the risk of missing major plot twists or important foreshadowing, I don't think this is related to Ann's background either...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Oceanids are sentient creatures unique to Fontaine, and they can create Oceanid creatures through mimicry and transformation.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: I remember all the strange and wonderful Oceanid creatures we saw before we met "Mary-Ann."

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Ann said the name sounded familiar. I should ask her about it should something come to mind.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: To Seymour, she is someone that he must protect.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Either way, ordinary humans don't live that long. It's been several hundred years, so they're probably not the same person, right?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Ann is a small Oceanid. She didn't create the Oceanid creatures in Annapausis.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Speaking of... Just how do Oceanids reproduce again?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Maybe Osial can create water creatures, but it's extraordinary to be able to imagine creatures with rich personalities.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: It's almost certain that there's an Oceanid in Annapausis controlling everything.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Who can she be?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The "Mary-Ann" in Annapausis seems very mysterious. We once suspected that Ann was a character from her dreams.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Ann's far too weak to control that whole realm, so she can't be the Oceanid behind it all.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: It's definitely not Ann. I believe her, she is also searching for answers.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Mary-Ann, who has the same name as Seymour's owner, and who seems to know everything.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Even if she's not an Oceanid, she's probably related to the Oceanid behind all of this.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Lyris isn't exactly the brightest Oceanid. She has lacks both the requisite power and madness to create Ann the Oceanid.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: A war took place inside Elynas, and many animals of steel and flesh died.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Seymour was damaged there and has been in the care of Mamere ever since.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Seymour's primary instruction is to protect "Mary-Ann."

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: We just confirmed that there is an Oceanid in Annapausis controlling everything.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Ann recalled a story, but we couldn't use its symbolism or metaphors as clues.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: But she does have memories that don't belong to her. How?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: If Seymour was damaged in Elynas, that means it likely failed in its mission, and the person that it was supposed to protect may have already...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: If Seymour failed, then perhaps that means Mary-Ann met with an unexpected misfortune during the conflict...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The person Seymour was supposed to protect was Mary-Ann Guillotin.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: This question must be answered eventually

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Where did Ann's memories of fairy tales come from?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: We can't just enumerate the possibilities and say it's Lyris and Mary-Ann Guillotin. That's disrespectful to Ann.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: But the Red Empress does appear in the fairy tales, and that's an element directly from the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Ignoring questions about lifespan and how long it's been, what happened to Mary-Ann Guillotin after Seymour failed?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The "Red Empress" is what the Narzissenkreuz Ordo called Lyris.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: She is the only other Oceanid involved in this whole affair.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: But she is not powerful enough to have possibly created Ann.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The intel we received said she was intellectually challenged, yet the "Mary-Ann" we saw seemed quite normal.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Can a kitten understand a little girl's thinking and behavior, and then have a vivid, life-like dream of its master? Probably not.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: We can speculate all we want, but we'll have to find Mary-Ann to find the truth.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Though I've got some vague ideas to go on, there are still things that I cannot convince myself of.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: I have to go see Mary-Ann in Annapausis to find more leads.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: I don't know why I can't get this out of my mind.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: This can't really be foreshadowing, can it?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: A member of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo from several hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Her whereabouts afterward are unknown.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: She is also the only other Oceanid involved other than Ann.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: "Mary-Ann," who wove a fairy tale without an ending...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: She refused our visit, but she mentioned her memories from the Narzissenkreuz Institute.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: It sounded like she was waiting for everyone to return to the Institute ruins.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The one that Seymour was supposed to protect.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Something happened in Elynas, resulting in Seymour's damage and her disappearance.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Where is she, and what is her relationship with "Mary-Ann"?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The only person who grew up in the Narzissenkreuz Institute and has a matching background is Mary-Ann Guillotin.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The person who once waited within the deserted ruins for everyone's return was Lyris, the former director.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: "Mary-Ann" has Lyris's memories.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: "Mary-Ann" has Mary-Ann Guillotin's memories.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: If so, then "Mary-Ann" is Lyris. Another piece of evidence we have is that they can both use Oceanid powers to control Annapausis.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: If so, then "Mary-Ann" is Mary-Ann Guillotin. They have the same name and matching memories.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: But how can she be both people at the same time?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: This must mean that Lyris, an Oceanid, probably has special powers.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Her job in the Ordo was to dissolve the members' egos. What could have happened between her and the missing Mary-Ann Guillotin...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: For some reason, Lyris dissolved Mary-Ann Guillotin's personality.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: And afterward, their wills, now mixed, began to dream.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: They dreamed of a simple world, where the princess is saved and the evil dragon gets killed, while the heroes are always pressing onward.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: They dreamed of a world where everything was simple and had an answer, as long as Ann was there.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Thus, Ann and "Mary-Ann" were born.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Let's come back in a few days, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Give them some time to sort both their bodies and memories out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whether it's Seymour's fragmented information, or Ann and Caterpillar... This is something only they can do for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a while. Let's go back to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and check on everyone.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: No, that can't be it...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: You return with everyone to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo...
